utterances.text: If we can lift the map up a little bit more before the witness marks it again. Little bit more. That's good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Balunovic, with the blue marker, if could you please again mark that line from Dobrici to Perica tor?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you go on the line on the left, if you can make it all the way, please, to Perica tor.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe were the line is ended, Mr. Balunovic, is Prgastine tor, and if you move a little bit more to the left, you'll see Perica tor. So if can you draw the line all the way there.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologise, what do you want me to write? I see here it says Prgastine tor and below that it says Perica tor. Oh, right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if you could just, please, to the right of the blue line with an X, just mark where the railroad line is.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next to that railroad line is a -- a road, correct, running from north to south? Parallel with -- to some extent, with the railroad line?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it on that road from Ramljane on the way to Knin, or somewhere in that vicinity near Ramljane, that you had the encounter with General Markac?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what road that was. I'm not familiar with the region. That is not where I was born. I was in that place only during that operation, never before, never after. It's very difficult for me to find my bearings on the map. I don't know what roads lead where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to have this document marked and moved into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D2040.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit D2040 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Balunovic, do you recall at all that this area in which you were operating on that day, to some extent, was very hilly and heavily wooded between the tracks where you marked as an X and the finishing point in Perica tor?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the configuration of the terrain there. But judging by the map, I would say that south of the axis there is an rather steep slope leading to an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with me - and tell me if you can or cannot - that the only thing what one would be able to see from the road or the tracks in the area of Ramljane, if anything, would be smoke, if smoke existed?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, there seems to be a suggestion in your question that it has got something to do with the previous question, which is rather unclear to me. Let's just see ... Now, first of all, if I re-read your question, whether Mr. Balunovic agrees with you, and he's invited to tell you, "... if you can or cannot - that the only thing what one would be able to see from the road or the tracks ... if anything, would be smoke, if smoke existed." Now he was first invited to agree with you or not that it was possible or it was not possible to see what you then described, and he agreed. I would say I would agree with that, as well, that it is possible or not possible. I'm just analysing your question and then to see what the answer is. And then -- but he can see smoke or not, what do you mean, that there was an officially obstruction or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is totally unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, from the train tracks and from the road, in the position of Ramljane, the only thing that one would be able to see from the roads or the tracks on the west side of that road, if there was fire, would be smoke. You wouldn't be able to see fires; you wouldn't be able to see anything burning. The only thing you would be able to see would be smoke; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So I can agree with you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, again, could we explore the base for this answer. Mr. Balunovic, why do you think that, to the west of the road or the track, if there was smoke, you only could see smoke and no fire? Could you tell us why that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I can remember, the terrain was forested. There were a lot of trees, in other words. And in that sense, I believe if -- if a house had been burning, one could not have seen the house from the trees but one could easily see the smoke coming from the -- the site, because the smoke would rise above the tree tops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kuzmanovic, there was -- I'm trying to further explore this, because we have not established yet anything about trees. You asked him questions about hilly terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I asked him, Your Honour, if the road and train tracks were heavily wooded and hilly in the area of the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I missed the "wooded." And if that is the case, I apologise for that. And, therefore, the answer by Mr. Balunovic is on the basis of the woods, rather than on the basis of the hills. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I asked him: Do you recall if this area in which you were operating on that day, to some extent, was very hilly and wooded between the tracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I understood that as woods on the hills. Perhaps that's a misunderstanding, but because in the next answer, because the hills didn't receive a positive confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't [Overlapping speakers] ... at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think, as a matter of fact, that the woods were not, at that moment, further dealt with in the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I asked both; was it very hilly and heavily wooded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you take me to the line exactly where that was. Well, I'll find it. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Why don't we pull up 65 ter 3D01001, please. Doc ID 3D070067. There we go. I don't know if we necessarily have to mark this, Your Honour, but this is a Google map of Ramljane, which we've discussed with Mr. Hedaraly. He doesn't have an objection to it, to give a top-down view of Ramljane.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, do you see on the right side there, the road and the railroad track?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mark that -- the road being marked with a 33.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me, just to the left of the road, there is what appears to be a fairly big hill with a number of wooded areas that runs from north to south?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it very clearly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I have a number for that document, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection. I don't know if it was done, but if we can just clarify for the record that that road is the Knin to Drnis road, the 33. I don't know if that was done or not. But we don't have no objection to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that was clear on the basis of the previous -- of the previous exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to make a little bit more clarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, the road that goes toward the top of the map goes toward Knin, and the road that goes toward the bottom of the map goes toward Drnis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already told you, I don't know. I'm not sure that that that's the case. I'm not very familiar with the area and that's why I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: To confirm it, we can pull P190 up, Your Honour, but I think under the circumstances, I don't think it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on P190, also the marked version, D2040, it -- there is hardly any doubt about whether this is the Knin-Drnis road. Mr. Registrar, the exhibit number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number would be D2041. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Kuzmanovic, one of my questions here is -- is what now exactly you can see or cannot see and where the woods are and what is meadow and what is not meadow. That's -- I have -- for example, if I look at -- to the right of that road, easterly direction, I see some darker green areas which, from my recollection, from what I see from a plane, resembles wood. But, if, for example, I would look from Ramljane or the road or the rail track close to that, to the west, I do not see similar things. So, therefore, I'm just asking myself, whether what kind of conclusions we are drawing on the basis of what exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is pretty, Your Honour, relatively easy to see if you combine this photograph with what is the map in P90 [sic]. You can see the elevations in P--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I -- let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And on this photograph from north to south, running immediately to the left of the road is -- you can tell by the switchback roads that is a hill that runs, basically, from north to south, west of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- I will have a closer look at the elevation lines that is P190. Because as witness said earlier, he said, I do not remember. What I see is that south of our track there is a -- a rather steep hill. When he said that, I looked at that map as well and I saw that the elevation lines, apart from that part where you go up 200, 300 metres, approximately, and I think Ramljane was at 563, but let me just check that, or 463. I'm just wondering what we really could and could not conclude from from this map, where the witness says that he has limited recollection. I'm just trying to get the relevant part of P190 on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I can fix this by my next set of questions, and, if I can't, you'll let me know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if I look at that road, and if I look to the west of that road, that I see one or perhaps two elevation lines. Whereas, between Dobrici and -- I see an elevation of 359 metres close to that, I hardly see any elevation lines in westerly direction. And I take it that one elevation line is - let me see - I don't know exactly how many metres that is. Would that be 10 metres or would it be ... I see that Mount Promina clearly is a feature, a hill with a lot of elevation lines; whereas, looking between Dobrici, in the direction of Perica tor, I hardly see any elevation lines. Again, the margin, south, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can understand that. The issue here is what can be seen from the road and the railroad track on this axis, Dobrici, Mijakovici, and Perica tor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm asking myself, because on the basis of a Google map which is, of course, a projection, you look from the top, so it's extremely difficult to establish what exactly the elevation difference is. You have some indications. For example, if you look at the road to -- from the road to Ramljane, then you see it doesn't go straight. It goes in a kind of a hairpin. So that may be an indication, not necessarily; whereas further south, we see that from that road, from the main road between Drnis and Knin, we see that a road stretches in a rather -- without any - how do you call it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Switchbacks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, it's -- to judge this on the basis of this map, which, apparently you're seeking to with the witness leaves, at least, some questions open. If you want us to adopt the conclusions, then get rid of those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. Perhaps we could take a site visit and go and take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, an application can be made. Well, not tomorrow because it might be difficult to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think can I explain this further using other documents as well as ones we've marked already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. I think it's good that you aware of me having some difficulties in following exactly what can be deduced from this map and from this Google Earth satellite picture. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could go to D4020 [sic] which was the map that was drawn on by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 2040, I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, there are a lot of green areas indicated on this particular map, Mr. Balunovic. The light green areas, does that represent to you areas that are forested or wooded, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, this axis which you described in your report, P770, Dobrici, Vujakovici, and Perica tor, you reported on, on -- in your written report of August 26th of 1995, and we'll get to that report and get it on the screen in a second. But you had written that your group came under fire from buildings in Vujakovici which is noted in the map along the blue line there from Dobrici onto Perica tor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would like to note that I have a very poor recollection of that action. Actually, there were many actions during the war and on similar terrain at that. As for this action, it was not discussed in such great detail during these questionings, so I really have forgotten quite a few details. I mean, right now, I cannot say for sure whether it was there exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please put up P770 on the screen. And, Your Honours, we're going to get the Google map elevation map out. Hopefully that will assist the Chamber. We're going to do that right now while I'm doing this questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, this is a report written in your handwriting dated August 26th, 1995, with your signature at the bottom; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's my handwriting and my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, on this document in part of the report, you said: "My group came under fire ... we returned fire with infantry weapons and anti-tank weapons, like a 64-millimetre RBR hand-held rocket-launcher." Before I ask, that is a Zolja, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you continue: "... which resulted in several buildings and haystacks catching fire." And that, you note, happened in Vujakovici. Now -- which is quite a distance from both the road and the rail line, would you not agree? According to the maps that we've seen.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it is according to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the fact that you were there, I know you don't recall very much about what happened on August 26th. But would you agree with me that if there was any kind of fire, as you reported in Vujakovici, the only thing that could be seen from the road or the rail line, based on the distance and the topography and the terrain, would be smoke?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to discuss - hopefully I'll finish by the break - the issue of General Markac and what he allegedly said to Mr. Drljo on the 26th. Now you said Mr. -- General Markac confronted the unit on the road. You're just not sure what road it was, but it was somewhere in the vicinity of Ramljane, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know whether Mr. Janic contacted General Markac and General Markac asked Mr. Janic what was up with the smoke?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Celic at all was contact -- in contact with General Markac regarding the smoke?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know about that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in your 65 ter OTP statement, at page 119 of 143, you noted that Mr. -- General Markac was upset because he had been informed that smoke could be seen from the train; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is what is written in the statement, then that is most probably what I had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And he didn't just come to confront the unit to say -- the Lucko Unit just to say hello, he was angry; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was quite angry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And on page 41 and 42 of your statement, you state: "I don't know if he spoke specially to the commanders, but Mr. Markac stopped our convoy. We exited our vehicles, and he spoke to all of us." And on page 42, you said: "I remember him being very angry. He was very strict, very abrupt." Now, you were aware, were you not, that there was a specific order that there not be any smoke or fire during this freedom train operation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that order exactly. But, of course, we had been warned that we should not do anything that would be against the law. So that had to do with the treatment of civilians and property. Of course, nothing should have been done that was against the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go back to your report, P770. The last sentence of your report says: "I would like to point out in this report that we complied with the order not to burn Serbian houses and nothing was deliberately set on fire." Now, your P770 report here specifically says that there was an order not to burn Serbian houses. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would like to say that if that is what I said in my statement, and my memory was fresh then, then I accept that that is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 7541, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Before we get it that document, did you verbally advise Mr. Celic that there was an incident of fire in Vujakovici before General Markac arrived? Meaning fire from weapons.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I informed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The document up on your screen, again, is a 16th of December, 2009, record of a witness interview in which you were cautioned that -- to speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And page 3 of that document, please. In the Croatian version -- or in the English version, the section starts, "The next day," which is about the middle of the way down. And I think it's the previous page in the Croatian version. I'm sorry, it's the next page in the Croatian version. English version is fine. Middle of the page: "The next day, we conducted a search." That's what I'd like highlighted, please. If we can match that up, please, with the Croatian version which is also in the middle of the page. About a third of way down, and the sentence is [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, we're talking about August 26th: "The next day, we conducted a search of the terrain in another part of the wider area of Knin. Some houses were set on fire in the field that day. I did not see who set those houses on fire, and I do not know the name of that place. I do not remember exactly, but it seems to me, it was on that second day at the so-called finish line. I'm not sure whether we drove before that or we were about to climb into vehicles when General Markac arrived and asked who set the houses on fire. I do not remember whether he mentioned a name of a village, but it seems to me that he referred to that village we passed through on the second day of the operation. As far as I remember, Franjo Drljo then angrily answered General Markac that he had set those houses on fire. Then, following an order by General Markac, we returned to the base in Lucko." Now, this statement differs somewhat from what you said in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. He was addressing the entire unit, was he not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now, I cannot remember all those details. But, again, I would like to say that I made that statement when my memory was fresh, when my health was better. I would accept what I had said then as -- as the truth, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could get P770 back up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, did I miss anything, that the fresh memory in -- weren't you reading from the 2009 statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and I'm going --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Couldn't we then see what the difference in freshness is between 2009 compared to 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I cited those already, Your Honour. Page 41 of 143 where I said: "I don't know if he spoke especially to the commanders, but Mr. Markac stopped our convoy, we exited our vehicles, and he spoke to all of us."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the reference to the statement was not the reference of the statement you had just read? Because you were -- you had just read the 2009 statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I did. And I'm going to use P770 to ask a question in juxtaposition of the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was a bit confused by -- if you quote a considerable portion of a statement. Well, he said, I would like to say that I made that statement, where you just had read the 2009 statement, then it came as a bit of a -- illogical, but if you are going to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P770, Mr. Balunovic, was written a day or two, or the same day of the action, was it not? August 26th, 1995, it is dated.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the day or the moment when I wrote that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It was certainly a day or two after the event that you described in the report, was it not? And it was certainly before December 16th of 2009 and November of 2004.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in this report, when General Markac confronted the unit and asked about the smoke, you had already had the information that you were going to put together for this particular report, that your group had come under fire from buildings and that these buildings, several buildings and haystacks, had caught fire. While Mr. -- while General Markac was berating the unit, about the smoke, why didn't you just tell him, Sir, we came under fire. We returned fire. Several buildings and haystacks caught fire. You didn't tell him that at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But you think I didn't do that because Mr. Drljo actually interrupted the discussion. I already said that Mr. Markac was quite upset. And I think that Mr. Drljo's outburst and his statement interrupted any further discussion in the field. After that, Mr. Markac was very offended, and he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you then tell General Markac, Look, it was the result of fire from our unit. Drljo had nothing to do with it. Were you covering for Drljo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I wasn't covering for anyone. I always behaved in a soldierly manner. I always waited to be asked. Before I answered or spoke. I didn't want to interrupt anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you, right after the action, let Celic know that there was some incident, so Celic could let General Markac know, verbally.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember whether I did that or not. I cannot say with certainty now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to your 2004 OTP statement, on page 118 and 119. There you describe this same August 26th incident. And you state: "I remember us walking down this road which was allegedly mined, and I remember going first with several of my men and Mr. Drljo and Mr. Krajina behind me. I can't remember Mr. Zinic. I do not recall exactly, I do not know exactly what happened, but allegedly some houses were set on fire. There was smoke coming from these houses." Now, you were with Drljo, according to your OTP statement of 2004. And in your report of August 26th, 1995, you describe several buildings and haystacks catching fire, as a result of return fire with infantry weapons. How can you reconcile those two, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that I said yesterday that I think that I wrote that report relying on assumptions for the most part. So there was shooting. At that moment I did not see any house catching fire, but I think that some houses did catch fire, so in the report, on the basis of an assumption, I wrote that that is how the fire happened, due to firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, your report says: "I commanded a group of 15 men," among other things. And it says: "My group came under fire while we were moving along the road towards that place. We returned fire." You are included in the group that you are discussing, correct? In P770.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: One final thing, Mr. Balunovic. When the discussion occurred where you heard about Mr. Sosa and Mr. Radocaj and the allegations about people being killed or -- in Grubori and -- and Mr. Drljo, that was in 2003?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the year. But it was -- well, I think it was at the time when investigators from The Hague Tribunal started their investigation. I don't know exactly what year that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You were still a member of the special police at the time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that had you heard something like you discussed and heard about Mr. Sosa and Mr. Radocaj, you had an obligation as a special policeman to report that to your commanding officer, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't think I would agree with you. Actually, it had to do with the following: People were being threatened, people who were my friends. I was being threatened. In addition to that, there is no statute of limitation on war crimes. So I thought it wasn't indispensable to take action with regard to that immediately. My friend Igor Radocaj said to me that he would testify. However, at that time, there was talk about Mr. Igor Beneta. There was a suspicion that he had committed some killings. It was being said that he had repented and that he was a collaborating witness. Igor and I came to the conclusion that nothing was needed yet, that things would be resolved, and that Sosa and he and I should not expose our families to the danger ever a possible revenge. That is why we decided to wait, because we believed that the matter would be resolved even without our intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: One last question and then I'll deal with the map after the break, Your Honour, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The elevation map, unless the Court [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I could cut that short. But please put your last question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, if the people on the ground at the time were not telling the truth about what happened, what were the people at the top supposed to believe about what happened, up the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. If I understood it correctly, I will try to give an answer. I think that the people at the top did not have any other information except for the information that could have been provided to them by people on the ground and possibly some other information, if there were some investigations under way that people had not been aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Balunovic. I don't have any further questions and

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Kuzmanovic, I find it important always to be as transparent as possible. That means that if we consult any source which is not in evidence that it should be clear to the parties that we have looked at it. Now, your suggestion that you could look at the elevation maps in Google maps, triggered me to quickly look at it. There, you find the information which gives a clue to how it is. If the parties could agree on the following. That is, that between the road number 33, between Knin and Drnis, which runs north to south, between that road and the village of Ramljane, which is at approximately close to half a kilometre distance from that road, that there is an kind of a ridge at an elevation at approximately 300 metres, running north to south, parallel to the road and the railway track. And that to the east of that ridge - that is, the elevation of the road and the railway track - that it's three elevation lines further down, which puts it at approximately 240 metres. Whereas, to the west ridge, descending, it's two elevation lines further down, which brings you to approximately 260 metres. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first would like to deliver a decision by the Chamber. The Chamber would now like to issue its decision concerning the Markac Defence motion for an order to prevent the Prosecution from relying upon Defence materials protected by Rule 70(A) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. On the 24th of February, 2010, the Markac Defence filed a motion for an order to prevent the Prosecution from relying on materials which it claims are protected by Rule 70(A). The document in question is a report titled: "Analysis of military police in Operation Storm." The report was prepared by the Croatian Ministry of Defence, in response to a Request for Assistance from the Markac Defence. In its motion, the Markac Defence argued that the document is protected by Rule 70(A), because it was prepared by the Ministry of Defence at the request of the Markac Defence, for the purposes of the proceedings before the Chamber. On the 4th of March, the Prosecution responded, requesting that the motion be denied. The Prosecution submitted that the document is not protected by Rule 70(A), because it was produced by the military police administration of the Ministry of Defence, and then distributed internally and archived by the Ministry of Defence. At the Prosecution's request, the Ministry of Defence provided the Prosecution with a copy of the document. Finally, the Prosecution argued that Croatian government organs and officials could not be considered a party's representative or assistants, as a result of a Request for Assistance or the receiving of such assistance. Under Rule 70(A), reports, memoranda, or other internal documents prepared by a party, its assistants, or representatives in connection with the investigation or preparation of the case, are not subject to disclosure or notification under Rules 66 and 67. The report in question was not prepared by the Markac Defence. Instead, the report was prepared by the military police administration of the Croatian Ministry of Defence. In its request to Croatia, the Markac Defence did not specify that it sought a report to be compiled for exclusive use by the Markac Defence. Furthermore, the parts of the report that have been filed before the Chamber do not indicate that Croatia intended such exclusive use. In fact, the report was distributed within and archived at the Ministry of Defence. It appears from the report that, when compiling the report, the Ministry of Defence considered itself to be acting in accordance with its obligation to provide assistance. Furthermore, Croatia also provided the Prosecution with a report at the Prosecution's request. Consequently, there are no indications that the Markac Defence, and Croatia agreed, that the report could only be used internally by the Markac Defence. In any event, it is not clear that such agreement between the Defence and a state could lead to a state becoming a member, assistant, or representative of the Defence in the sense of Rule 70(A), or whether such agreement would be consistent with a state's obligation towards the Tribunal under the Statute. Be that as it may, in the present case, the Chamber concludes that the mere fact that the report was prepared pursuant to a Request for Assistance from the Markac Defence does not turn the report into an internal Markac Defence document in the sense of Rule 70(A). Consequently, the Chamber finds that the report does not fall within the scope of Rule 70(A), and, accordingly, the Chamber denies the Markac Defence motion. And this concludes the Chamber's ruling on this matter. I would now like to give a statement in relation to the Brioni transcript P461. The Chamber would like to address the transcription and translation of the Brioni transcript, which is in evidence as P461. On the 1st of April, 2009, the Gotovina Defence filed a revised version of the Brioni transcript, pointing out shortcomings in the transcription and translation of P461. On the 15th of April, 2009, the Prosecution responded, agreeing to only four minor corrections of P461 and objecting to all the other modifications proposed by the Gotovina Defence. On 20 January 2010, the Chamber instructed the Gotovina Defence to send to CLSS certain parts of P461 for verification and to get back to the Chamber as soon as CLSS had sent the results. On the 12th of February, 2010, the Gotovina Defence filed a memorandum compiled by CLSS and containing eight transcription and translation clarifications. In order to have in evidence a faithful transcription and translation of the meeting held in Brioni on the 31st of July, 1995, P461 should reflect the corrections set out by CLSS and filed by the Gotovina Defence on the 12th of February, 2010, as well as the four minor corrections conceded in the Prosecution's request [sic] to Ante Gotovina's submissions regarding P461, Brioni transcript, which was filed on the 15th of April, 2009. At the same time, the Chamber is mindful that P461 has been discussed with several witnesses in this trial, and therefore considers important that the original version of P461 remains traceable in the evidence, for the purpose of fully understanding and properly assessing the relevant evidence of those witnesses. To this end, the Chamber invites the Gotovina Defence, which had originally moved for a revision of this exhibit, to do the following: The Gotovina Defence should upload into e-court a new version of P461, both in B/C/S and in English, with the CLSS memorandum attached. First, that new version should include an annotation, in both the English and the B/C/S transcripts, wherever a part of the meeting was not transcribed; and each annotation should clearly and correctly reference the relevant part of the CLSS memorandum. Second, the new transcripts should reflect the corrections conceded by the Prosecution in its response. Three of these corrections concern a wrongly identified speaker, while one concerns the omission of a press release read out by President Tudjman. The Gotovina Defence should make annotations in the transcripts precisely reflecting these changes. As far as the first two steps are concerned, the Chamber invites the Gotovina Defence to look at Exhibit P2526 as an example of how to proceed. The Chamber emphasises that it must be clear, to the extent possible, exactly where missing text should be inserted. Third, the new English transcript should reflect the corrections in translation made by CLSS. These corrections should be typed in bold, reflecting exactly what is contained in the CLSS memorandum. The Chamber stresses that, when annotating P461, all text should appear on the same pages; thus, avoiding any confusion with regard to page numbers. Fourth, the new document, comprised of the new transcripts and the CLSS memorandum, should be uploaded with the following title: Presidential transcripts of meeting held in Brioni on 31st of July, 1995, including modifications as agreed by the parties and references to the attached CLSS memorandum in relation to disputed portions of the original transcription and translation. Once the documents have been up loaded, the Gotovina Defence shall notify the Chamber as well as the other parties, who will have one week to raise any objections they may have. After that, if no objections are raised, the Registry is hereby instructed to substitute the present version of P461 with the newly uploaded version and to notify the Chamber, as well as the parties, when it has done so. And this concludes the statement on P461. The third item on the agenda is the 1991 census. The -- when the parties have made -- had invited the parties to make submissions on the admission of the 1991 population census in its entirety, the Gotovina Defence responded that it would be beneficial to all parties if they were informed of the purposes for which the census was intended to be used before it would make submissions. In an e-mail, dated the 13th of April, 2010, the Chamber observed the following: That was an e-mail addressed to the parties. Under Rule 89(C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, admission of a document depends on relevance and probative value. With respect to relevance, the Chamber notes that the 1991 population census provides data on the size of the population and its ethnic composition for specific areas in the Republic of Croatia in 1991. Such data may provide context and/or corroboration to other evidence before the Chamber and assist it in making factual determinations relevant to the indictment. The Chamber is aware that the census data relate to 1991 and emphasises that any decision on admission would not be an indication of the weight, if any, which the Chamber may ultimately attach to the census and its content. In that same e-mail, the parties were invited to make any further submissions, not later than the 20th of April, which is today. Is the Chamber to expect any further submissions by today or ...
